steps.description: Four things to set before your first visitor arrives. This takes about five minutes, and you can leave at any point — nothing here is locked in.
steps.title: Welcome to Visitor Management

steps.description: VMS Settings holds the policy everything else reads: how far ahead a visit can be booked, how long an invitation link lives, the meal windows that decide hospitality, and the colours on the visitor's own page.
steps.title: 1 — Set the ground rules

steps.description:
Visitor Type is the important one. Each type names the role that approves it, and that single field builds the approval workflow — contractors to one role, candidates to HR, VIPs to two approvers in sequence.

Add your own types freely; the workflow rebuilds itself.
steps.title: 2 — Decide who approves whom

steps.description: Visitor Gate should match the doors you actually have. Point each Visitor Type at its usual gate and security sees the right one already filled in.
steps.title: 3 — Name your gates

steps.description:
Visitor Invitation sends a private link. Your guest fills in their own details and uploads their ID, and the pass arrives in the approver's queue.

No mail server yet? The link is shown on screen so you can send it yourself.
steps.title: 4 — Invite someone

steps.description: From here, Visitor Pass is the working record, Security Log is the gate, and Daily Visitor Log shows who is expected today.
steps.title: That's the setup
